To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
brain derived neurotrohic factor (BDNF), and insulin like growth factore-1 (IGFI) induced neuroprotective effect in spinal cord injury is influenced by mechanisms that involve nitric oxide (NO).

brain derived neuro-trophic factor and insulin-like growth factor-1 pretreatments significantly reduce the upregulation in the expression of neuronal nitric oxide synthetase (nNOS) and cell injury in the rat spinal cord following injury.
BDNF or IGFI induced neuroprotective effects in spinal cord injury may be mediated through the down regulation of nNOS activity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of BDNF and/or IGF in the pathogenesis of spinal cord injury and its possible therapeutic application.
the possibility of the neurotrophic factors to reduce the upregulation in the NOS activity in the spinal cord following trauma.
the role of BDNF and/or IGF in the modulation of NOS activity following spinal cord injury.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BDNF and/or IGF-I induced neuroprotection in spinal cord injury is probably mediated by the inhibition of NOS activity.
the growth factors BDNF and insulin-like growth factor-1 are effective in reducing the upregulation in nNOS expression, edema formation and cell death following trauma to the rat spinal cord.

BDNF or IGFI pretreatment significantly reduced the up regulation of NOS in the spinal cords and this neuroprotection is probably associated with a reduction of edema and cell death following trauma to the rat spinal cord.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BDNF/IGF induced neuroprotection is mediated by the inhibition of NOS activity in the spinal cord after trauma.

the neurotrophins BDNF and IGFI have the capacity to protect the spinal cord from secondary injury following trauma and that these neuroprotective effects are mediated, at least partly, by the regulation of nNOS.
neurotrophins may be a potential therapeutic tool for spinal cord injury.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth factors BDNF and insulin like growth factors are neuroprotective in the spinal cord and may exert their neuroprotective effect via regulation of nNOS activity.
BDNF, IGF and other neurotrophic factors may be useful as therapeutic agents for the treatment of acute spinal cord injuries.
BDNF/IGF may be used in conjunction with NMDAR antagonists to provide a neuroprotective effect following trauma to the central nervous system.
